children.counts: Count out loud: knee-knee, clap-clap, partner-partner.
children.game_version: Play the Heel-Toe Polka focusing on the rhythm game of slapping knees, clapping own hands, and clapping partners' hands before stepping to a new friend.

seniors.counts: Count in steady 4/4 or 6/8 walking beats matching the musical bars.
seniors.seated_version: Perform Heel-Toe Polka rhythms while seated by tapping knees, clapping hands, and clapping hands with a seated partner.
seniors.standing_version: Walk the spatial paths in longways or circle formations at a steady walking pace without brisk turns.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Execute figures at a moderate walking tempo with compact arm movements during claps and holds.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Ballroom hold in closed-couples formations; partner hand slaps and knee slapping in polka sequences
movement_profile.footwork: Less emphasis on complex foot work and more about people being in the right place
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Big circles, Sicilian progressive circles, longways sets of 3 to 8 couples, trios, and quadrille squares
movement_profile.partnering: Couples facing, side-by-side trios, alternating circle positions, and frequent progression to change partners
movement_profile.posture: Relaxed social posture suitable for folk hall movement

signature_moves.description: Dancers slap their own knees, clap their own hands, and slap both hands against their partner's hands.
signature_moves.name: Heel-Toe Polka Slap Sequence

signature_moves.description: In The Ninepins Quadrille, four couples dance while a spare person is left unpartnered and playfully mocked by the set.
signature_moves.name: The Drongo Partner Exclusion

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Over-focusing on intricate footwork instead of maintaining line-of-dance progression and group spatial position

music_profile.meter: Reel, jig, march, waltz, and hornpipe meters
music_profile.musical_form: Traditional UK and Irish folk dance tunes arranged for bush band
music_profile.sound_description: Bush dance music is driven by the melodic interplay of fiddle, accordion, concertina, or tin whistle over the rhythmic strumming of guitar or banjo, grounded by bush bass and percussive rattle from the lagerphone. The tunes comprise traditional Irish and British dance melodies played in reel, jig, march, waltz, or hornpipe meters.

basic_steps: Progress to next partner around the set
teaching.formation: Big circles, closed couples, longways sets, Sicilian circles, trio lines, and four-couple quadrilles
teaching.level_notes: Accessible to beginners; emphasis is on floor position, progression, and group timing rather than technical foot precision.
teaching.rhythm: Reels, jigs, marches, waltzes, and hornpipes
